boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Calvin University destinations for research, group work, art, recreation, science, and time outdoors, each supported by a direct university source.

cards.title: Choose a study setup across five floors
cards.subtitle: Research help, collections, carrels, tables, and group rooms
cards.notes: Use the floor maps to choose among tables, carrels, and study rooms, then ask library staff for research assistance.
cards.short_summary: A five-floor academic library with more than one thousand documented study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin states that Hekman Library supports scholarship with research assistance and has 1,037 study spaces, including tables, carrels, and study rooms across five floors.
cards.access_notes: Library hours vary by academic calendar; consult the library's current open-hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Meet where student services and study space overlap
cards.subtitle: A shared gathering and collaboration area inside Hekman Library
cards.notes: Settle into a gathering or study area, then use nearby student services when your project needs practical support.
cards.short_summary: The renovated library hub combines collaborative space with student organizations and support offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin says the Hekman Library renovation created Commons Union gathering and study spaces and centralized student services and organizations on the library's 200 level.
cards.source_title: Hekman Library - Construction at Calvin | Calvin University
cards.access_notes: Commons Union is inside Hekman Library; some extended periods require a Calvin student or staff card.

cards.entity_name: H. Henry Meeter Center for Calvin Studies
cards.title: Work directly with specialized Reformation sources
cards.subtitle: Fourth-floor research center in Hekman Library
cards.notes: Take the elevator to the fourth floor and use the center's databases or staff expertise for focused primary-source work.
cards.short_summary: A specialized research center with physical collections and Calvin-related scholarly databases.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin identifies the Meeter Center on Hekman Library's fourth floor and provides its Calvin Resources Database, Post-Reformation Digital Library, and library catalog for research.
cards.source_title: The H. Henry Meeter Center | Calvin University
cards.access_notes: Academic-year hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m., with a noon–1 p.m. closure; summer hours differ.

cards.title: Take coursework or reflection onto the trails
cards.subtitle: Trailed woods, ponds, vernal pools, and meadows on east campus
cards.notes: Stay on the public trail network, bring course observations or a notebook, and leave the restricted sanctuary undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A campus preserve where public trails coexist with teaching, research, and protected wildlife habitat.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin documents 40 trailed acres open for exploration, including forest, ponds, vernal pools, and meadows, while identifying the Buiten Wildlife Sanctuary as restricted research habitat.
cards.access_notes: Public walking trails and restrooms are open daily from 7 a.m. to dusk; remain outside the restricted wildlife sanctuary.

cards.title: Study beside the preserve's field resources
cards.subtitle: Laboratory classroom, multipurpose room, and display hall
cards.notes: Use the display hall to review Great Lakes flora and fauna, or ask preserve staff about student-group space.
cards.short_summary: The preserve's educational building doubles as a study center for the university community.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin describes the Bunker Interpretive Center as a 5,000-square-foot study and educational center with a laboratory classroom, multipurpose room, and display hall.
cards.access_notes: The center is accessible; weekday building hours and holiday closures vary by season. Student groups should contact preserve staff about reservable space.

cards.title: Compare native habitats bed by bed
cards.subtitle: Demonstration gardens beside the Ecosystem Preserve
cards.notes: Follow the paths and scan the bed-specific QR codes to compare native species, habitat types, and seasonal changes.
cards.short_summary: A mapped collection of native demonstration beds with paths, plant lists, and views toward South Pond.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin says Venema Plaza & Gardens contains more than 40,000 native plants representing over 200 species, with habitat-themed beds, paths, and QR-linked descriptions and plant lists.
cards.source_title: Native Gardens - Ecosystem Preserve | Calvin University
cards.access_notes: The gardens are part of the preserve complex; use public paths during posted preserve hours.

cards.title: Inspect minerals under more than visible light
cards.subtitle: Minerals, fossils, meteorites, and an ultraviolet display in North Hall
cards.notes: Start with the fluorescent-mineral case, then compare the Michigan specimens, meteorites, and fossil displays.
cards.short_summary: A compact geology museum where specimens reward close, side-by-side observation.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin documents a rotating collection of more than 500 specimens, including minerals, fossils, meteorites, native copper, and fluorescent minerals, with free admission.
cards.source_title: Bruce Dice Mineralogical Museum | Calvin University
cards.access_notes: Located in North Hall room 162. Seasonal hours apply; informal student-docent tours are offered during open hours.

cards.title: Use a changing exhibition as a visual prompt
cards.subtitle: Temporary and student exhibitions in the Covenant Fine Arts Center
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition before arriving, then bring a sketchbook or discussion question for a focused visit.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery where temporary shows support observation, discussion, and cross-disciplinary learning.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin says the Center Art Gallery presents temporary exhibitions by visiting artists and Calvin students, faculty, and alumni in 3,800 square feet of exhibition space.
cards.access_notes: The gallery follows the academic calendar and closes to the general public during summer; verify the current exhibition and hours.

cards.title: Put class astronomy through a real telescope
cards.subtitle: Campus dome used by students from introductory through advanced courses
cards.notes: Choose a clear scheduled evening, confirm weather conditions, and follow the posted North Hall rooftop directions.
cards.short_summary: A working educational observatory with scheduled student access and public Wednesday viewing.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin states that its campus observatory has an educational mission, is used by students at all levels, and opens to Calvin students on clear weekday evenings during fall and spring semesters.
cards.source_title: Calvin Observatory Physics and Astronomy | Calvin University
cards.access_notes: Access is weather-dependent and limited to posted sessions. The dome requires stairs; portable-telescope viewing can be arranged for wheelchair access.

cards.title: Learn the wall with trained instruction
cards.subtitle: A 40-foot indoor wall in the Spoelhof Fieldhouse Complex
cards.notes: Bring a signed waiver, check in with staff, and use the first-timer training before attempting belayed routes.
cards.short_summary: A student recreation space with changing routes, supervised sessions, and beginner instruction.
cards.evidence_claim: Calvin documents a 40-foot-tall climbing center with more than 50 changing routes, trained instructional staff, first-timer training, and free access for Calvin students, faculty, and staff.
cards.access_notes: Only Calvin students, faculty, and staff may use the center. Climb solely during staffed program hours after completing the required waiver and instruction.
